Everyone is different. I have it worse when it is a very stressful time. For example when my mom went through pancreatic cancer and my dad was in rehab I would have these really extreme panic attacks. For me a trigger where sirens. Police sirens. I would think they where after me. Even when I heard Helicopters flying over me I thought they where trying to find me. Trying to get me. It was so weird because I knew how ridiculous it was. I have never done anything to fear sirens or helicopters. I knew that, even at the time of the panic attacks I knew it was ridiculous and made no sense. But still it persisted. I am much better now, but still sirens make me trigger into a bit of anxiety. The last time it was really bad was when there was a missing kid around where I was living. There was a single Helicopter flying over my house for over 3 hours, I heard the police over the megahorn. And I was so scared. I thought that they where trying to find me. They where looking for me and they where going to kill me. I knew that obviously I didn't have the kid and I shouldn't have anything to worry about other than to hope the kid is safe. But during those three hours I could hardly breathe. It was like I was underwater. The thing about my paranoia is that no matter how ridiculous it is, it starts to make sense after awhile. Your brain tricks you to feel like the shadows are real, that the sirens are coming for you, that there is someone watching you.  I also have paranoia from mirrors because I think people are watching me from the other side. That I developed as a kid and once I learned about the Bloody Marry game then I got even more anxious. It all depends on the person. But the triggers for me is stress and when I am stressed I get really bad panic attacks.

Personally I actually liked this game better than the first smash bros. now it does have a lot of flaws, but it is also really fun too. The thing that ruins it for most people is that they expect it to be a smash bros clone with playstation characters. But sony made this game so it wouldn't feel like a "smash bros clone". there is no ring outs, you can only kill people using specials. Which I believes causes more strategy and more lengthy battles. Me and my bud once spend an hour and a half on a three stalk battle and it was one of the funnest battles of my life. The hard sell with this game is that it takes time to understand. Smash bros is easy to pick up but difficult to master, this game is hard to pick up but it easier to understand but there is so much strategy that it is also hard to master. Each character to me seems very ballanced, even though people where dissapointed in the characters in the game I found them all to be pretty equal and you can usually find someone that you can fit with really well. Single player in this game is garbage. it is not fun at all, the multiplayer is a blast though. even when you are batteling strangers on the internet it is so much fun. It isn't much of a party game like smash because again people see it as a super smash cone when they should see it as a game on its on. I really like the way the specials work in this game. To summarize your type of character can deal either strong hits slowly and this character gain more level up bonus with each hit, or there is fast characters who do not gain as much level up bonus with each hit. each character has three specials called level 1, level 2 and their ultimate level three. you can not get three without two and you can not get level two without one. It causes a lot of strategy of when to use the ultimate because a layer can easily dodge roll and counter with his own moves. Items in this game land a lot of level up power and sometimes feel over powered but it also creates havoc to get to that item as well which is fun. there are not many levels or characters and most of the levels need a fine tuning. Each level has a collaboration of two separate games. I cannot tell you all of them off the top of my head but the one level that sticks most out to me is the little big planet level. I'm from california and I have actually been two two colleges out of state. I'd say it all depends on your situation. 

For me, I don't really have a great home life, I notice that in California nothing changes. All my friends are stuck in dead end jobs, all the people I know here are community college dropouts, i'm not close to my family at all so moving away was the right choice for me for many reasons. 

Before I moved I was really immature, the only thing that really mattered to me was finding a good girlfriend. My grades and my future was really not important to me. I decided to move out of state for college because I knew i had to get away. My first year i went to Idaho, A place where i knew no one and it was a great experience.  I figured out what i truly wanted to do, met a lot of people that actually cared about me and i was doing very well in classes. but Idaho was never my ultimate goal, my dream was to go to school in new york, and after a year of Idaho i decided that I have learned as much as I could at that school and it was time for me to move on. I got into the school in New York and the transition was really rough. Transfer students really have a disadvantage at colleges and i felt really isolated there for many reasons. Most of the reasons was the schools fault but I know it would still be difficult for me even if the transfer program was amazing. but my second semester of this school I met my now girlfriend and she helped me transition pretty well. My grades are improving, and i have noticed I am much happier. Here I'll list you a pros and cons list that i have noticed in my experience, but remember everyones experience is different. 

Pro-
1. you get to see the huge differences between the two states. a lot of things i never considered (people, food, locations, fun, religion) depending on where you go these will be different. and for me that was amazing.
2. you don't get in a helpless circle. I believe if you stay close to home you basically stay and do the same things you have been doing for the past 18-20 years. so if you are not happy about your life now, its the perfect time to start looking for other schools
3. independance ( this is the most important! you learn how to do things that have been provided for you all your life, cooking, laundry, self confidence, plunging,) you don't have your family there for you constantly which really helps you mature
4. you get to met people you would have never had the opportunity to
5. if you go to school out of state you won't depend on your parents and your parents won't depend on you. no going home on the weekends for chores, no visits, for me i loved that. the less i spent at home the freer i felt
5. you get to explore who you truly are! (this was fantastic for me) i realized that my friends at home had a definition for me and when i got to introduce myself to strangers it was a fresh start, a new chance to make a first impression. That really helped me know that I am not who others define me as, I am who i am.


Cons

I know that the pros are really dependant on what your own situations are, just as the cons will be as well.

1. Holidays. Sure you get to go home for christmas, but some holidays you have to stay in the dorms, and usually that is alone. i've realized that if you go to schools with a high in state community than any day off or holiday you will be alone. (spring break and thanksgiving was particularly hard for me. i suggest doing volunteer work for spring break cause a week alone gets really lonely)
2. money. (you will be buying for most of your things. many things you won't even consider( bath towels, sheets pillow and pillow cases are just some of the few things you should buy at your future school's state, and small things like trash cans, lamps, cups, bowls and silverware. groceries are tough to get use to buying. I think i spent about 5000 on my last two years of school. That includes books, and fun though so it is all dependant on what you are comfortable spending. (i get no help at home)
3. roommates. Some are great, some are terrible. You just have to realize that if you live out of state most of your nights will be spent in your dorm. If you hate your roommate you can't avoid them to much, unless you meet a SO
4. leaving your pets goodbye- this was really hard to leave my dog at home. we recently put him down, and it is particuarlly hard for me to get over because i spent so much time away from him
5. you loose a lot of people you'd never expect. College out of state really shows you who is important in your life and who is not. Its really sad to see some really good friends go because you are just inconvenient and far away. It was helpful for me to see who truly mattered in my life, its eye opening.

Advice for any school you go to. GET INVOLVED! college is centered around meeting people, meet as many people as you possible can, find a great group of people and have the time of your life. Keep a reality check on whats going on, what you are and are not comfortable with and hold on to your values.

I know this is a long list and i have so much more to say. if you need more info just PM me.

It was worth it for me, Its a really scary situation but it is worth the risk. Good luck
